title: HTTP status codes are never appropriate — every response returns 404
evidence: src/main.cpp:27 registers only setDefaultHandler and never addHandler, so server.cpp:169 handlers_.find() always misses and control falls to the default branch at server.cpp:174-177 which hardcodes status_code=404. handleRequest (src/handler.cpp:136) returns only a body string, so 201/400/404-semantic codes are impossible; server.cpp:172-173 would hardcode 200 for a matched handler but none are ever matched. Result: successful GET /books, POST /books, and even GET /health all return HTTP 404.
suggestion: Have handleRequest return a status code alongside the body (or register real routes via addHandler) and pass it to generateResponse; return 201 on create, 400 on validation failure, 404 for missing book.

title: GET /books emits malformed JSON — isbn string is unterminated
evidence: src/handler.cpp:211 serializes the list element ending with `<< jsonEscape(book.isbn) << "}"` — the closing quote of the isbn string is missing, producing `"isbn": "<value>}`. The correct single-book path at src/handler.cpp:264 ends with `<< jsonEscape(book.isbn) << "\"}"`. Any client parsing GET /books receives invalid JSON.
suggestion: Change line 211 to `<< jsonEscape(book.isbn) << "\"}"` to close the isbn string, matching line 264.

title: Server integration tests self-skip get/update/delete assertions
evidence: tests/test_server.cpp:138, 172, 206 print `SKIP:` and bypass the get-by-id / update / delete assertions when create returned no ID over HTTP — the HTTP path is not actually verified end-to-end, consistent with the README-documented 'Known Issue' in _agent_stdout.log about POST body handling.
suggestion: Fix the HTTP layer so create returns an ID over the socket, then make these assertions unconditional.
